reproduction_target: Residue-level calibration of missense variant effect predictors: curation of ClinVar-derived datasets (ClinVar_HQ, well-annotated ClinVar proteins, ClinVar_BM, ClinVar_AFM) and the ProteinGym clinical substitution benchmark; residue attribute annotation (disorder via ALBATROSS Metapredict v1.3, protein-protein interface via PIONEER, homolog count via UniRef clusters, physico-chemical properties); ESM1b log-likelihood-ratio scoring with sliding-window extension for long sequences; Gaussian-Mixture-Model modelling of class-conditional score distributions; Jensen-Shannon divergence between subgroup entropy distributions; logistic-regression per-subgroup calibration; benchmarking of 23 VEPs via Ensembl VEP and precomputed EVE/AlphaMissense scores; the RaCoon calibration-tree pipeline (partition, prune, GMM model, bin, map); ablation, leakage and hyper-parameter experiments; and the public RaCoon web-server model ensemble. No wet-lab component.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis from the 'Online Methods' prose. Dataset curation is split into the four named datasets plus ProteinGym because each has distinct filters and provenance. Score normalization and JSD estimation are folded into one step (both are SciPy/numpy post-processing on the same score tables). Reliability histograms, ECE, MCE, AUROC/per-protein AUROC and Youden-J thresholds are folded into one 'classification/calibration metrics' step. The four RaCoon algorithms (partition, prune, model, bin/map) are folded into one pipeline step. Code axis is scored from the code-availability statement and the public repository landing page/README prose only; no source file was read line-by-line (stage-2 work). Version axis reflects prose pins only: the sole software version pin anywhere in the paper is 'ALBATROSS Metapredict v1.3'; the repository's requirements.txt (visible in the README run instructions) lists numpy/pandas/scipy/scikit-learn/torch/metapredict, and its unpinned nature is recorded as a floating capture claim, not as an environment lock.

steps.label: ClinVar_HQ curation: ClinVar GRCh38 VCF downloaded July 2025; records missing CLNSIG/CLNVC/CLNREVSTAT/CLNHGVS excluded; single-nucleotide missense retained; N=171,196
Well-annotated ClinVar protein subset: sequences with >=10 variants including >=4 pathogenic and >=4 benign; N=1,285 transcripts
ClinVar_BM benchmark subset re-used from Radjasandirane et al. 2025 (circularity/annotation-bias-minimized ClinVar subset) for the 23-VEP benchmark
ClinVar_AFM subset construction to avoid AlphaMissense calibration circularity with ClinVar_BM
ProteinGym zero-shot clinical substitution benchmark obtained June 2025; provided protein sequences used, labels assigned from the benchmark
Score computation for the 23 benchmarked VEPs (Table 3) using Ensembl VEP, except EVE and AlphaMissense queried from published precomputed datasets

Disorder annotation with ALBATROSS Metapredict v1.3; disorder precomputed per residue for all isoforms of reviewed human UniProt proteins and all dataset transcripts; residues with score > 0.7 defined as disordered (vs suggested 0.5)

Protein-protein interface residue prediction with PIONEER; high-confidence interface predictions for all reviewed human UniProt sequences (repository ships pioneer_predictions.zip per landing page file list)
Homology stratification by direct query of UniRef sequence clusters; 'few homologs' defined as UniRef90 cluster size < 10
Physico-chemical residue attribute assignment (polar, hydrophobic, aromatic, sulfur-binding, etc.) with predictors and thresholds specified in Table 4

ESM1b LLR scoring (wild-type marginals; softmax over log-odds at the variant position) plus wild-type / mutant / masked representation entropies; sliding-window extension for sequences exceeding the 1,024-token context
Mutual information between residue attributes and pathogenic labels with scikit-learn mutual_info_score (residue level) and three-bin protein-level grouping; 1,000 non-parametric bootstrap iterations

GMM fitting over LLR scores: modified z-score outlier removal (|z| > 4.25), balanced sampling, scikit-learn GaussianMixture with two components and diagonal covariance, remaining parameters default; component count chosen by BIC plateau

Per-subgroup logistic-regression calibration: percentile outlier removal (top/bottom 0.1 percentile), balanced sampling, scikit-learn LogisticRegression with L-BFGS solver and otherwise default parameters; one third of data used for calibration, two thirds for testing

Cross-model score normalization (modified min-max after 0.1-percentile outlier removal, orientation flip check, outliers reinstated at 0/1) and Jensen-Shannon divergence between subgroup normalized-entropy histograms (100 equal-width bins, smoothing, squared JS distance; bin-size sensitivity at 200/100/50/25 bins) using the SciPy implementation

Discrimination and calibration metrics: global and per-protein AUROC, Youden-J optimal thresholds (1,000 bootstrap iterations), reliability histograms with 10 equally spaced bins, weighted Expected Calibration Error, Maximal Calibration Error over bins with >50 samples

RaCoon pipeline (Algorithms 1-5): calibration-tree partitioning by protein length then greedy JSD-maximal attribute splits; pruning at MIN_VARIANTS_PER_LEAF=1600 / MIN_PATHOGENIC=400 / MIN_BENIGN=400; per-node pathogenic-fraction estimation from 500 sampled labels; per-node GMMs trained on 400 pathogenic + 400 benign; equal-frequency calibration histograms built from 40,000 synthetic GMM draws; inference-time leaf assignment and bin mapping

Ablation, data-leakage and hyper-parameter experiments: single and pairwise feature ablations, seen-vs-unseen balanced split leakage test, GMM training-size and synthetic-sample/bin-count sweeps (100 independent GMM training iterations each averaged over 100 non-parametric bootstrap resamples); Fisher exact test with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR and SciPy mannwhitneyu two-sided tests

RaCoon public server ensemble: predictions averaged over the median of 75 of 100 randomly initialized RaCoon models trained on ClinVar_HQ, with per-prediction standard deviations and node-specific ECE/MCE (https://bio3d.cs.huji.ac.il/webserver/racoon/)

headline.static_readiness: 0/19 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 1/19 (5%) RI at stage-1. Data availability is strong (all study datasets deposited at Zenodo record 17690936, plus public ClinVar/ProteinGym/UniProt/UniRef sources) and a public code repository exists (https://github.com/sapir-amittai/RaCoon, Python, README with a runnable command line), so the data and code axes reach 2 for the core calibration steps. The binding constraint is the version axis: the only software version pin anywhere in paper or README prose is ALBATROSS Metapredict v1.3, and the repository dependency manifest visible from the README run instructions is unpinned (numpy/pandas/scipy/scikit-learn/torch/metapredict, no ==). Every step therefore caps at version 0 except C7 (version 1), so 18 of 19 steps fall to NI even under an inference-inclusive reading of code coverage. Closing the version gap alone (pinned environment or container) would lift roughly 13 steps to RI; R-star would still require stage-2 execution.
headline.coverage: 19 computational steps assessed from the Online Methods prose plus the Data availability and Code availability statements. No wet-lab steps (W = 0); the paper is entirely computational. Repository assessed at landing-page/README-prose level only; no source file was read.

gaps.where: Software environment for every computational step (C1-C19)
gaps.missing: No lockfile, conda environment, or container is claimed in the paper or the README. The repository's requirements.txt, referenced by the README's 'pip install -r requirements.txt' instructions, lists numpy, pandas, scipy, scikit-learn, torch and metapredict with no version constraints. The paper's only software version pin is ALBATROSS Metapredict v1.3; ESM1b (checkpoint), Ensembl VEP, PIONEER, scikit-learn, SciPy and PyTorch are all unversioned. Results depending on scikit-learn GaussianMixture / LogisticRegression defaults and on SciPy's Jensen-Shannon implementation are therefore not version-anchored.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a resolved environment (pip-compile/uv lock, conda-lock, or a container digest) alongside the repository, and state the exact ESM1b checkpoint identifier and Ensembl VEP release used.

gaps.where: Upstream feature computation and benchmarking (C1-C6, C8, C11, C19)
gaps.missing: The code availability statement covers 'all code used to implement RaCoon'. The repository landing page shows the calibration pipeline (main.py, gmm_utils.py, tree_node.py, consts.py, utils.py, data_classes.py, mutation_record.py) plus a benchmarking_and_analysis directory, but the README documents only the calibration entry point and describes clinvar_balanced.parquet as shipping precomputed ESM1b scores, entropy and disorder annotation. Whether the dataset curation (ClinVar VCF filtering to ClinVar_HQ), the ESM1b LLR/sliding-window scoring, the 23-VEP Ensembl VEP benchmark, and the server ensemble are covered by released code cannot be established from the README prose.
gaps.how_to_close: Document in the README which scripts regenerate each dataset and each figure, and include the ClinVar curation and ESM1b scoring entry points (or state explicitly that precomputed tables are the intended reproduction path).

gaps.where: C6 VEP benchmarking; C12-C18 stochastic procedures
gaps.missing: For the 23-VEP benchmark, no Ensembl VEP command line, cache release, plugin set, or transcript-selection rule is given, and the retrieval date for the precomputed EVE and AlphaMissense score sets is not stated. For the sampling-heavy procedures (balanced sampling, 100 GMM initializations, 1,000 and 100 bootstrap resamples, 40,000 synthetic draws) no random seeds or seeding scheme are reported, so numeric values such as AUROC 0.912 -> 0.924 are not bit-reproducible from the prose.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the VEP invocation (version, cache, plugins, transcript rule) and the retrieval dates for the precomputed score sets, and record seeds or a seeding policy for the sampling/bootstrap loops.

gaps.where: Precomputed residue annotations (C7, C8) and derived dataset tables (C1-C5)
gaps.missing: The paper states that all datasets are available at Zenodo record 17690936, and the repository additionally ships clinvar_balanced.parquet and pioneer_predictions.zip, but the Zenodo record contents are not enumerated in the paper and there is no per-file mapping from figures/tables to deposited files. The proteome-wide Metapredict disorder precomputation and the PIONEER high-confidence interface set are described in prose without stating which deposited artifact carries them.
gaps.how_to_close: List the Zenodo file inventory in the data availability statement with a figure-to-file mapping, and state which deposited file holds the precomputed disorder scores and PIONEER interface predictions.
